title: Orange Revolution
summary: The runoff of the Ukrainian presidential election of November 2004 was awarded to Viktor Yanukovych on a count that observers and much of the country rejected, and Kyiv's Independence Square filled for two months until the Supreme Court ordered the vote rerun; Viktor Yushchenko won it. It was the largest of the post-Soviet electoral revolutions and it delivered less than it promised: the winners quarrelled, the reforms stalled, and the man the square had turned out was elected president in 2010. That disappointment is not a footnote to it — it is why the square filled again nine years later.
